newsitem.title: CANADA: NOVA plots Alberta pipeline expansion.
newsitem.headline: NOVA plots Alberta pipeline expansion.

text.p: NOVA Corp unit NOVA Gas Transmission Ltd, the main mover of gas in Alberta, said on Tuesday it planned to spend C$1.4 billion through the year 2000 expanding its pipeline network.

In its annual plan filed with the Alberta Energy and Utilities Board, NOVA said the expansion program would add 2.25 billion cubic feet per day of delivery capacity to its system while maintaining flat unit costs.
The company's pipeline network, which for decades has had a near monopoly on gas transport in Alberta, moves more gas each day than any other system in North America.
But NOVA's dominance in Alberta has recently been threatened by a number of competing pipeline proposals, including the Alliance Pipeline, Alberta Pipeline Project and Crowsnest Pipeline Project

NOVA said the facilities would be installed throughout the province, and that the plan demonstrated its "aggressive management of its costs," which were not projected to rise over the next four years.
"This plan is clear evidence of NGT's continued responsiveness in the competitive environment," NOVA Gas Transmission vice-president Russ Wells said in a statement.
"The expansion meets the producing industry's need for increased capacity. At the same time, we will continue to keep unit costs on our system flat."

The company said its expansion plans were focused on the 1997/98 gas year and the winter heating season of 1998/99 and included gas-flow assumptions adjusted to better reflect historical and projected use of gas storage.
NOVA said it was working with downstream gas transmission companies, which are expanding, to coordinate approvals and timing. It was also continuing to secure shipper commitments.
The system currently transports more than 12 billion cubic feet of gas a day, representing about 18 percent of North American supply.
